paper.title: Cross-scale covariance for material property prediction
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes a statistical approach to predict large-scale material properties—specifically plastic flow strength in FCC metals—from small-scale 'indicator' properties computed using the same interatomic potential (IP), by quantifying cross-scale covariance. Using a pool of 178 IPs (reduced to 153 after screening), it identifies highly covariant small-scale predictors (e.g., C44 elastic constant, unstable stacking fault energy, vacancy migration energy) via correlation analysis and k-fold cross-validation, builds multi-linear regression models, and applies them to DFT-computed small-scale predictors to estimate flow strength with quantified uncertainty bounds.

task.task_name_raw: Predict plastic flow strength from small-scale indicator properties
task.objective: Estimate plastic flow strength of FCC metals using regression on small-scale indicator properties computable at quantum-accurate (DFT) scale, with quantified prediction uncertainty.
constraints: Predictor properties must be computable at small scales (≤10² atoms) where DFT is feasible
Same interatomic potential must be used for both large-scale MD and small-scale indicator calculations
Statistical pool must be representative and unbiased
input_requirements: Small-scale indicator properties (e.g., elastic constants, surface energies, vacancy formation/migration energies) computed with the same IP
Large-scale MD-simulated plastic flow strength values for statistical pool
output_goal: Regression model mapping small-scale indicators to plastic flow strength
Quantified prediction error bounds (e.g., RMSE, ±2×RMSE) for DFT-based predictions

evidence.text: Here we explore covariance between predictions of metal plasticity, from 178 large-scale (~108 atoms) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and a variety of indicator properties computed at small-scales (≤102 atoms). All simulations use the same 178 IPs. In a manner similar to statistical studies in public health, we analyze correlations of strength with indicators, identify the best predictor properties, and build a cross-scale “strength-on-predictors” regression model. This model is then used to estimate regression error over the statistical pool of IPs.

As a test bed in the material simulation context, we examine the covariance of dislocation-based plastic flow strength in face-centered cubic (FCC) metals (our QoI) computed in large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with indicator properties of the same materials computable on small scales, e.g., elastic constants, surface energies, etc.
We use multi-linear regression to illustrate the construction of a statistical model relating flow strength to the indicator properties

stages.stage_name_raw: Collect large-scale MD strength data and small-scale indicator data from OpenKIM
stages.stage_goal: Acquire plastic flow strength values from large-scale MD simulations and small-scale indicator properties for 178 IPs from OpenKIM repository.

evidence.text: The IPs used are available in the OpenKIM repository at https://openkim.org4 along with their predictions for a range of material properties computed using robust and vetted computational protocols.
All non-DFT small-scale property calculations in the present work were performed by the OpenKIM Processing Pipeline.

stages.stage_name_raw: Exclude IPs with numerical instabilities or anomalous crystal response
stages.stage_goal: Remove IPs exhibiting numerical instabilities or qualitatively abnormal plastic response (e.g., crystal rotation, phase transformation, SF jamming) to ensure statistical pool homogeneity.

evidence.text: MD simulations using one particular IP could not be completed due to numerical instabilities encountered irrespective of the integration time step. Another 14 IPs were excluded after subsequent analyzes revealed anomalies or irregularities in crystal response to straining, such as crystal rotation, phase transformations, and formation of amorphous phases, or voids...

stages.stage_name_raw: Clean and impute missing/unreliable small-scale indicator data
stages.stage_goal: Address missing or out-of-bounds values in the small-scale indicator dataset for the remaining 163 IPs by computing missing values, re-computing unreasonable ones, and applying k-nearest neighbors imputation.
stage_input: 163 IPs' small-scale indicator data with missing/unreliable values

evidence.text: Inspection of small-scale indicator properties of the remaining 163 IPs, precomputed in the OpenKIM repository, revealed some missing or out-of-bounds values deemed unreliable. Out of 62 initially considered indicators, 27 properties contained numerous missing or unreliable values and were excluded from our study altogether. To fill the gaps in the 163 × 35 table of the remaining small-scale properties, wherever possible we (1) computed the missing property values, and (2) re-computed property values falling outside of their physically reasonable range.

stages.stage_name_raw: Exclude IPs exhibiting stacking fault jamming
stages.stage_goal: Remove IPs showing 'stacking fault jamming' — a qualitatively distinct plastic mechanism — to preserve statistical homogeneity of the QoI.
stage_output: 153 IPs remaining after SF jamming exclusion

evidence.text: Of the 16 models that were identified as SF jammed, six had been previously excluded from the statistical pool based on other considerations. Outliers or not, we excluded all SF jammed IPs from further statistical analyses on the grounds that they exhibit a plastic response qualitatively different from the rest of the remaining IP models, thus paring our statistical pool down to 153 IP models

stages.stage_name_raw: Develop and compute new vacancy-related indicator properties
stages.stage_goal: Generate new candidate small-scale indicators related to vacancy energetics (formation energy, migration barrier, formation volume) based on physical insights from MD defect analysis.
stage_output: Four new vacancy-related indicator properties added to candidate set

evidence.text: Analysis of the defect microstructures observed in MD simulations suggested additional indicator properties not previously included as possible predictors... Following this logic, we developed new Open-KIM property calculations (KIM test drivers) for computing the vacancy formation energy (both relaxed and unrelaxed), the vacancy migration barrier, and the vacancy formation volume... Thus, they were added as candidate independent variables in subsequent statistical analyses, bringing the number of available indicator properties to 39.

stages.stage_name_raw: Select top-performing predictor combinations via k-fold cross-validation
stages.stage_goal: Identify the most informative subset of small-scale indicators (1–3 variables) for regression by evaluating all 9919 combinations using repeated k-fold cross-validation on the 153-IP pool.
stage_output: Top-performing 3-variable predictor combination: {111} surface energy, lattice constant, vacancy migration energy

evidence.text: Figure 4b presents one of the best 3-variable regression models... fit the 153 samples remaining in the statistical pool with the adjusted goodness of fit parameter r2 = 0.88.

stages.stage_name_raw: Train multi-linear regression model on selected predictors
stages.stage_goal: Fit a multi-linear regression model mapping the selected small-scale predictors to plastic flow strength using the 153-IP statistical pool.
stage_input: 153 IPs' values for {111} surface energy, lattice constant, and vacancy migration energy

evidence.text: Figure 4b presents one of the best 3-variable regression model (see the figure caption for details), fit the 153 samples remaining in the statistical pool with the adjusted goodness of fit parameter r2 = 0.88.

stages.stage_name_raw: Estimate prediction error using leave-one-out cross-validation
stages.stage_goal: Quantify the regression model's prediction uncertainty by performing leave-one-out cross-validation on the 153-IP pool.

evidence.text: As an estimate of the prediction error by regression on DFT predictors, the average relative prediction error among 153 leave-one-out models is 15%.

stages.stage_name_raw: Predict flow strength from DFT-computed predictors
stages.stage_goal: Apply the trained regression model to DFT-calculated small-scale predictors ({111} surface energy, lattice constant, vacancy migration energy) for seven FCC metals to obtain flow strength predictions with error bounds.
stage_input: DFT-computed {111} surface energy, lattice constant, and vacancy migration energy for Ag, Al, Au, Cu, Ni, Pd, Pt
stage_output: DFT-based flow strength predictions for seven FCC metals with ±2×RMSE error bars

evidence.text: We used FP DFT calculations to compute the predictor properties used in the 3-variable regression model shown in Fig. 4b, i.e., the {111} surface energy, the lattice constant, and the VME. Figure 5 shows the flow strength of seven FCC metals Ag, Al, Au, Cu, Ni, Pd, and Pt, predicted by substituting into the regression model the three predictors computed for each metal using DFT.
